problems.prompt: What is the key physical difference between electrophoresis and electroosmosis?
choices: Electrophoresis moves the charged particle itself; electroosmosis moves the bulk fluid via the wall's double layer
Electrophoresis moves the fluid; electroosmosis moves the particle
They are identical phenomena with different names
Electroosmosis only works with neutral particles and no field
problems.explain: In electrophoresis, the field acts on the particle's own charge in a stationary fluid. In electroosmosis, the field acts on mobile ions in the electric double layer at a charged wall, dragging the bulk fluid — which then carries any suspended particles, even neutral ones.

problems.prompt: What determines whether a particle experiences positive or negative dielectrophoresis (DEP)?
choices: The sign of the Clausius–Mossotti factor (particle vs. medium polarizability)
The sign of the particle's net electric charge
The direction of the applied field only
problems.explain: DEP does not require the particle to carry net charge. The Clausius–Mossotti factor compares the particle's polarizability to the surrounding medium's; a positive value pulls the particle toward high-field regions (positive DEP), a negative value pushes it away (negative DEP).

problems.prompt: Dielectrophoresis requires a ____ electric field, whereas electrophoresis works even in a uniform field.
problems.explain: DEP arises from the gradient of E², so the two poles of the induced dipole feel unequal forces. In a perfectly uniform field the forces on the dipole cancel and there is no net DEP force. Electrophoresis instead acts on a real net charge, so a uniform field alone produces a steady drift.
